summary: Dedicated pool mis-accounting causing queue starvation and automated fallback to lower-capacity models
description:
Issue summary:
Customer on Dedicated pool (NeuronFlow) observed sudden queue growth and automated fallback to smaller/cheaper model variants during a traffic surge on 2026-03-10. The pool reported available GPU capacity, but allocation latency spiked and multiple requests timed out waiting for slot assignment. This caused our routing layer to trigger fallback policies and route traffic to lower-capacity models, degrading quality for the customer.

Impact:
- Customer p99 latency increased from ~220ms to ~8.2s for their reserved routes.
- Significant increase in failed allocations (allocation_timeout), leading to 15% of requests falling back to smaller models for ~45 minutes.
- Customer-facing errors: increased 5xx and degraded output quality during fallback period.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: neuronflow-dedicated-pool-12
- Region: prod us-west
- Affected model routes: redwood-13b-v1 (primary), llama2-70b-q4 (fallback candidate)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Tenant sent a burst of ~6k short streams (average payload 256 tokens) over 2 minutes starting 2026-03-10T14:02:00Z.
2) Autoscaler reacted and provisioned additional nodes, but resource-manager recorded transient NVLINK error on 3 GPUs.
3) Serving runtime reported slot accounting mismatch: free_slots reported >0 but allocation requests remained unfulfilled for ~30-60s.
4) Router triggered configured fallback (route to smaller model family) when allocation latency exceeded threshold.

Observed behavior:
- Queue depth climbed to 420 requests (baseline <50).
- Allocation latency p50/p95/p99: 200ms / 2.1s / 6.9s during spike.
- Resource-manager logs show repeated "Lease reconciliation timeout" and "slot_mark_inconsistent" warnings.
- KV-cache hit rate dropped for the tenant due to frequent short streams.
- Noisy tenant pattern: many short-lived connections with high-frequency cold starts.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should provision capacity without causing allocation mis-accounting.
- Slot accounting should reflect true available GPUs; requests should either be queued with transparent progress or allocated to warm nodes instead of triggering fallbacks prematurely.

Logs / metrics referenced:
- Grafana panels: dedicated/neuronflow/pool-12/allocations (spike @14:02)
- Resource-manager logs: /var/log/rv-resource-manager/neuronflow-2026-03-10.log (errors: Lease reconciliation timeout 14:02:12Z, slot_mark_inconsistent 14:03:05Z)
- SLO dashboard: route redwood-13b-v1 showed fallback rate 15% between 14:02-14:47

Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Race in resource-manager reconciliation path caused transient negative accounting; autoscaler saw pods as scheduled while resource pool hadn't finished NVLINK recoveries, leading to "ghost" free-slots that were not usable.
- Hypothesis 2: High churn of short streams evicted KV-caches and increased GPU context-switch overhead; combined with NVLINK errors this amplified allocation latency.
- Evidence: resource-manager logs show 1.8k lease re-sync attempts in the affected window, and kernel driver reported NVLINK flapping on 3 GPUs for ~4 minutes.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support: throttled noisy tenant by applying shorter burst limit on their reserved routes to smooth the inbound traffic (applied 2026-03-10T14:20Z).
- SRE: increased warm-pool minimum for neuronflow-dedicated-pool-12 to 20% while we reconcile (applied 2026-03-10T14:30Z).
- Resource-manager: restarted fleet-agent on 4 nodes to clear stuck leases (rolled restart at 14:35Z).

Next steps / proposed fixes:
- Engineering to add stronger reconciliation and double-check slot state before reporting free_slots to router. See linked PR for an initial fix.
- Add guard against triggering fallback until allocation latency passes a longer probe window when pool has recent reconciliation errors.
- Evaluate NVLINK error handling: ensure nodes with NIC/NVLINK transient failures are marked unhealthy earlier.

Customer impact and follow-up:
- Customer impact window: ~14:02 - 14:47 UTC on 2026-03-10.
- CS engaged with NeuronFlow; they reported impact to end-users (summary attached in comments).
- Post-incident: schedule 1:1 with customer to review root cause and compensating credits if required.
